title: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: What Makes One Work | AIVideosUGC
description: UGC means a clip that looks like a creator made it. Make one from a photo or a product link, with words, a voice, and a person on screen. Not a real customer.
h1: AI UGC Video Ads Guide: Creator-Style Clips for Your Shop
lead: A UGC ad should feel like a person talking about the jar, not a studio spot. Start from a photo of what you ship, or from the public listing. You still read the line before it goes out.
secondary_keywords: short video ads for small brands
summary: How a shop turns one jar photo, or the public listing, into a short ad that sounds like a person talking.

sections.h2: What This Tool Builds for a Shop
paras: You leave with a short ad for the gray skincare jar: a script, a presenter, and an edit, from the photo or the public listing. Nobody has to visit the storeroom with a camera.

Publish it on [Instagram](page:plat-instagram), [Facebook](page:plat-facebook), or [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok). A feed post of the jar can be square at 1:1. A full-screen story wants 9:16. 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4 are available when the placement asks for them.

sections.h2: See What a Creator-Style Ad Looks Like
paras: A tall clip of the jar fills a phone, a square file sits in a scrolling post, and a wide file fits a larger screen.
The pictures use one jar so you can see the hand, the lid, and the shelf. Your file should do the same: the jar you ship is the jar in the opening frame.
sections.alt: Hands choose between two views of plain gray skincare jar on a bathroom shelf.

sections.h2: Reasons to Make the Jar Ad Here
paras: Written from the jar you sell. If the jar is one ounce, the line can say one ounce.
Ready for a placement you pay for. A Reels placement wants the jar tall. A feed post can take the same jar as a square. Ask for 9:16 or 1:1, and use 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 when that placement asks.
More than one style in a run. One cut can talk about how the cream feels on the skin. Another can open on the lid coming off. Keep the one that matches the jar you sell.

sections.h2: How to Make a Video Ad in 3 Steps
paras: Name the action first, such as a hand lifting the lid. Then paste the listing, or type one sentence about who the jar is for.
You get a clip back with someone speaking. The line can say how the cream sits on the skin, which is something you can show.
Save the file and put it in the ad account you already use for that jar. If the placement is a story, use the tall file. If it is a feed, use the square one.
Paste the listing in [URL to video](page:url-to-video), or choose the face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors). A second opening is another job from the same jar photo.

sections.h2: What Should the Clip Start With?
paras: Open on the jar already doing something, with the item already in a hand as it leaves the tote.
For this jar, show the lid twist or the jar lifted onto the counter. One action per clip. Ten seconds has room for that moment and a glimpse of the bathroom.
sections.alt: Hands pull plain gray skincare jar from a tote onto a bathroom counter.

sections.h2: How Long Should the Ad Be?
paras: Use 6 or 10 seconds for one action with the jar, 15 when the cream has to be used, and 30 for a fuller showing. Pick 9:16 so the clip fills the phone.

Six seconds is a lid coming off and costs 24 credits. Ten seconds fits that action plus a second look and costs 40. Fifteen can take the jar out, use it, and set it down, and costs 60. Thirty leaves room for a longer showing and costs 120. You see the number before you start.

Use 1:1 for a square scrolling post, 16:9 for a wide screen, and 3:4 or 4:3 when the placement asks for that shape. Each length or shape is a new clip. For a clip of the jar in use, start with [product videos](page:product-videos).
sections.alt: Hands close plain gray skincare jar on a neutral bedroom dresser.

paras: The file includes the spoken line, captions, and music you are allowed to run in an ad. Read the captions before you publish, and fix a wrong word before the ad goes live.

Put the words in the upper middle of a tall video, away from the app buttons at the bottom and the right edge. Use a face from the actor library and a logo you own. The [Content Policy](/content) says what can be uploaded.

sections.h2: Can I Present the Avatar as Someone Who Bought It?
paras: No. The face is generated, so the line stays on the jar and how the cream is used.
Make another version when you want a different room or a different first action with the same jar.
You can post from the jar photo or the public listing, at 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Read the line before you post.
A finished clip can run in ads, and the download has no watermark.

faq.q: What does a video-ad tool build for a shop?
faq.a: A tool that makes a short ad for a product you already sell. You bring the jar photo or the listing, and you get a file with someone speaking. This guide walks through each step.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad with AI?
faq.a: Start with the jar photo. Say the first action is the lid coming off. Download the tall file if the ad is a story, or the square file if it sits in the feed.

faq.q: Who is an AI video ad tool for?
faq.a: A shop that needs an ad for each product it sells this month. It is a poor fit when you only want one filmed founder story.

faq.q: Do I pay before the first ad?
faq.a: No. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Each job shows its credit cost before it starts.

faq.q: Can I run the file as a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. A paid plan includes commercial use, so you can put the file in an ad account, and the download has no watermark.

faq.q: Which shapes and platforms can I use?
faq.a: Wherever the ad runs. [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts) and [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) want a tall 9:16 file. A square 1:1 file can sit on [Facebook](page:plat-facebook) or [Instagram](page:plat-instagram). 16:9, 4:3, and 3:4 are there when the placement names them.

faq.q: Can I make ads for many products?
faq.a: Yes. Run a batch across the products you choose. Each clip shows its credit cost before it starts. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Do these stand in for a creator?
faq.a: Use a generated clip when the jar needs three openings this week. If buyers only trust the founder, film the founder for that one product and use generated clips for the others.

faq.q: Will TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram reject the ad?
faq.a: These apps do not ban a generated ad as a category. They do care if the clip pretends a stranger bought the jar. Read that app's current ad rules before you spend, and read our [Content Policy](/content) for what you can upload.

faq.q: What if the clip shows a part my product does not have?
faq.a: Make the clip again and name the exact action and the exact jar in the sentence, so the lid and the shape match the photo.
